key_insight: Full-spectrum deep learning detected separator contact defects during copper laser welding, with LSTM achieving the highest reported separator F1-score of 0.99.
engineering_relevance: Spectroscopic monitoring could help identify separator contact that risks thermal damage and safety issues in lithium-ion battery production.
method: Evaluated fiber core diameter, slit width, optical configuration, and integration time for spectroscopic monitoring.
Trained LSTM, GRU, CNN, TCN, and CNN+LSTM models to classify normal welds and separator contact defects.
Compared characteristic wavelength bands (350–450 and 650–750 nm) with the full spectrum (232–1110 nm).
evidence_signal: Separator F1-scores were 0.87–0.88 for characteristic wavelength bands and 0.91–0.99 for the full spectrum.
watch_item: The abstract does not report dataset size or independent production-line validation, leaving deployment generalization uncertain.
paper_title: Detection of Separator Contact Defects Using Spectroscopic Signals and Deep Learning in Copper Laser Welding for Lithium-Ion Batteries
